title: Preserving Symmetry: Spontaneous Symmetry Breaking through Decoherence
abstract: Solids appear to have localised centres of mass, yet many-body quantum theory describes them using translationally symmetric models that preclude localisation. Conventionally, this is resolved through spontaneous symmetry breaking by introducing an interaction with a semiclassical environment that breaks the symmetry. In the thermodynamic limit, the interaction can be removed while leaving the state localised. This, however, raises the question of how localisation arises outside the thermodynamic limit, i.e., in finite quantum systems (Wallace, 2018). Here, we show that, by quantising the environment, the localisation of finite systems occurs within decoherent branches, while the state vector of the composite system remains translationally symmetric. Our approach is analogous to the Page-Wootters construction (Page & Wootters, 1983) and quantum reference frames; moreover, we recover the semiclassical description as a limiting case while predicting experimentally distinguishable corrections away from this limit.
summary: This theoretical paper resolves the conflict between observed particle localization in solids and the underlying translational symmetry of quantum mechanics. By quantizing the environment, the authors show that apparent symmetry breaking occurs only within localized 'decoherent branches,' while the total system state remains globally symmetric. This offers a finite-system resolution to long-standing issues in condensed matter theory.
main_problem: The paper addresses how localized centers of mass appear in solid materials, reconciling this observation with quantum mechanical descriptions that are fundamentally translationally symmetric.
main_result: Localization arises within decoherent branches when the environment is quantized, allowing the total state vector to remain globally translationally symmetric.
method: The authors analyze the system-environment coupling by quantizing the environment and examining the reduced density matrix dynamics relative to the environment's position.
model_or_system: The model involves $N$ interacting particles (the system) coupled to a harmonic oscillator environment. The Hamiltonian is analyzed in terms of center-of-mass and environmental degrees of freedom.
key_observables: Ground-state width ($\sigma_{	ext{pin}}$), reduced density matrix off-diagonal terms, and the relative state $|\psi(x)angle$.
important_parameters: Environmental mass ($M_0$), coupling strength ($\mu$), and system size (finite vs. thermodynamic limit).
main_assumptions: The core assumption is that quantizing the environment allows for a description where decoherence causes apparent symmetry breaking without violating global symmetries.
paper_structure: The paper contrasts conventional semiclassical approaches (relying on environmental potentials) with the novel approach of quantizing the environment. It develops mathematical tools to define relative states and shows how decoherence leads to localized branches while preserving global symmetry.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous quantum mechanical framework for understanding emergent classical-like phenomena, such as localization, using decoherence theory in a way that respects fundamental symmetries.
